newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia sees 1996 inflation below 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia sees 1996 inflation below 10 percent.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Friday that the country's inflation rate for 1996 would be below 10 percent, while GDP growth would top four percent.
"The latest economic indicators are very good and show that inflation will definitely be below 10 percent, while GDP growth will be above four percent," Drnovsek told a news conference.
In August the annual inflation rate fell to 10.3 percent from 10.7 percent in July.
First quarter 1996 GDP grew 1.09 percent, compared to a fall of 0.33 percent in the last quarter of 1995.
Late last year the government said it expected inflation for 1996 to slow to six percent from 8.6 percent in 1995, while GDP growth was projected at five percent, up from 3.52 percent in 1995.

The government was forced to change its projections in May following a series of public sector strikes that forced Drnovsek to ease his tight anti-inflation policy. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
